brief: A black cat on the homepage first screen faces the visitor and its eyes follow the pointer. Its tail runs down behind the page and peeks out at the very bottom; pull it too hard and the page snaps back to the top while the cat jumps in fright. The page itself stays as it is: paper, ink, Literata, e-ink refresh.

candidates.name: 01 Photo cat
candidates.concept: A real cat that wandered into the same greyscale photography as the workbench, sitting on the hero rule.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated greyscale photo, white background dropped with multiply
Sits on the hero rule in the gap between the words and the photo
Tail hangs over the rule and vanishes below it
Pupils are code-drawn vertical slits that track the pointer
Startle: swap to a puffed-fur frame plus a code-driven jump

candidates.name: 02 Ink cat
candidates.concept: A few strokes of sumi ink, perched on top of the photograph with its tail dropping behind it in one brush line.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated ink-wash painting, ink density becomes alpha
Crouches on the photo's top edge; the photo drops ~130px to make room
Tail goes behind the photo, so 'hidden behind the page' is literal
Ties to the History frame (rubbings, thread-bound book)

candidates.name: 03 E-ink cat
candidates.concept: A 1-bit dithered cat that looks like it lives on the e-reader screen, sitting on the baseline of whichever word is lit.
candidates.typography: Unchanged: Literata 400/300 italic for the three words, IBM Plex Mono 400 for labels
traits: Generated photo turned into Atkinson dither, 110 dots wide, pixelated
Sits on the baseline of the lit word; can hop to the next word as frames rotate
Pupils are square dots that move one cell at a time
Startle uses the site's own e-ink refresh flash
Most on-concept with the Refresh direction
